intro: One large cup of milk bubble tea with normal sugar has about 350 kcal (estimate). Most of it comes from sugar syrup, tapioca pearls and milk creamer.

variants.name: Brown sugar milk tea with pearls
With pudding or cheese foam added

diet: Yes, but treat bubble tea as a snack, not just a drink. 350 kcal is roughly the same as a small plate of rice. Once a week with less sugar can still fit into your daily calories. What makes weight loss hard is drinking it almost every day without realising.
tips: Choose 25% or 50% sugar. After a week, your tongue will get used to it.
Pick a medium size, or share a large cup with a friend.
Swap pearls for jelly, or go without toppings to save calories.

swap.name: Medium milk tea, 25% sugar, no pearls
swap.why: You still get the milk tea taste, but with less than half the calories because the sugar and pearls are cut down.

faq.q: What are bubble tea pearls made of?
faq.a: They're made from tapioca (cassava) starch. They're almost all carbohydrate and are usually soaked in sugar syrup.

faq.q: Does 0% sugar mean no sugar at all?
faq.a: Usually it means no added sugar syrup. But the creamer, milk and toppings still have their own sugar.
Yes, if it's made with black tea, green tea or oolong. If you're sensitive to caffeine, avoid drinking it late afternoon or at night.
